svg.title: Normal invariant center pairings force an invariant probability
svg.desc: A K1 invertible over the first-jet graph algebra gives the normal central functional L u of z, the matrix sum of delta u evaluated on z u inverse. Dilation invariance makes it an invariant normal functional. If nonzero, its finite positive total variation normalized by its mass is an invariant normal state of the core center. The no-invariant-state hypothesis forces L u to vanish, and the real Thom and Morita isomorphism forces the circle two-trace to vanish on every K0 class. The lower panel shows exact integer intervals in the real coordinate of a semifinite core center. Each has the same mass m. Finite sums imply m zero; normality makes their increasing union have mass zero, contradicting probability.
svg.metadata: Original CC0. Lemma 13.12, Theorem 13.13, Corollary 13.14 and equations (13.49),(13.55)-(13.58). Human sources: Connes 1986 Theorem 7.14; Connes-Takesaki 1977. Abstract center has no pictured point-space model. The bottom line is the actual real coordinate in the semifinite tensor center.
svg.text: The center-valued argument applies to every analytic K-class
First-jet core: N = Cφ(M), Z = Z(N)
θs = β−s, δ(b) ∈ N_*, δ(b)(z) = 0 for z ∈ Z
δ(b) is normal; fixed first-jet support kills its derivative density almost everywhere.
No invariant normal state ⇒ Lu = 0 ⇒ Jψ = 0 on K₁(B)
m₂Φ₁¹ is an isomorphism ⇒ Jτ = 𝔉 = 0 on all K₀(A)
Semifinite model: Z = Z(M) ⊗ L∞(ℝ), with translations
Translation carries each interval to the next.
Finite disjoint sums: km ≤ 1 for every k ⇒ m = 0.
